sources.title: Camidge et al. ALTA-1L final results
sources.setting: 275 ALK-inhibitor-naïve advanced ALK-positive NSCLC patients randomised to brigatinib 180 mg after seven-day 90 mg lead-in vs crizotinib 250 mg twice daily.
sources.snapshot_note: Primary indexed abstract checked with current search and open; final-analysis date also checked in downloaded current EMA SmPC section 5.1. No individual prognosis or statistically conclusive OS advantage asserted.

sources.title: Gettinger et al. ALTA final long-term analysis
sources.setting: 222 crizotinib-refractory ALK-positive NSCLC patients: arm A 90 mg daily (n112) vs arm B 180 mg after seven-day 90 mg lead-in (n110).
sources.limitations: Phase 2 dose-arm study, not a different-drug comparator or a modern ALK inhibitor ranking. Do not confuse investigator PFS (15.6/9.2 months) with IRC (16.7/9.9).

sources.title: Ahn et al. Real-world treatment patterns and subsequent treatment effectiveness following frontline brigatinib in ALTA-1L
sources.setting: 48 selected patients following brigatinib discontinuation, including 40 given subsequent systemic therapy.
sources.limitations: Retrospective chart review excludes those continuing brigatinib and is not a full-population randomised update. Added as a scope qualification, not replacement PFS/OS or superiority evidence.

source_conflicts.nccp: Avoid strong and moderate CYP3A inhibitors.
source_conflicts.smpc: No routine adjustment for moderate inhibitors, with close monitoring.
source_conflicts.resolution: Visible Consultant/pharmacy review; no silent source precedence or invented dose.
Numeric field explicitly NCCP CrCl; document method discrepancy and pharmacy review. No silent interchange or calculated conversion.
